key_features: Asymmetric, irregularly bordered brown lesion with multiple colors (light/dark brown, blue-gray, pink-red), central blue-white/gray structureless area, atypical network at periphery and irregular dots/globules at the left edge.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark blue-black blotch, irregular peripheral brown dots and globules, a blue-white veil-like area, and uneven pigment distribution on sun-damaged skin.

Light-brown lesion with central hyperpigmentation, a faint reticular network fading symmetrically to the periphery, and a few small central dark dots, all without blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a benign (possibly dysplastic) nevus, though the slightly irregular border keeps some risk.

Small irregular, asymmetric brown lesion with uneven pigment, a blue-gray/black focus at the lower pole, and a blurred edge, on sun-damaged elderly skin, raising concern for early melanoma (lentigo maligna type), though the small size keeps uncertainty high.

Light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly uniform, faint reticular pattern, central hypopigmentation and soft fading borders on sun-damaged skin, without blue-white veil, atypical dots or irregular streaks, favoring a benign nevus, though the mild asymmetry keeps some uncertainty.

An asymmetric, bilobed light-to-medium brown lesion with an irregular, fuzzy border, an irregular network and streak-like projections, scattered peripheral dots and globules, and central regression-like whitish-gray areas, which together favor early melanoma over a dysplastic nevus.

The lesion is elongated and somewhat asymmetric with lighter brown extensions, but its fairly organized dark-brown central globular, cobblestone pattern fading to a uniform light-brown periphery, without blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, favors a nevus.

Dark, irregular pigmentation surrounding follicular openings (facial pseudonetwork) with asymmetric, partly obliterated openings, gray areas, and a whitish regression-like zone suggests lentigo maligna, though this image alone cannot confirm it.
Fairly symmetric reddish-brown lesion with a relatively uniform pigment network and dots, mild border irregularity, and no blue-white veil or regression structures, most consistent with a nevus.

Small (~4-5 mm) lesion with a central white scar-like patch surrounded by a delicate peripheral brown pigment network, typical of a dermatofibroma, with no atypical network, streaks, or blue-white veil.

Small, light-to-medium brown lesion with mostly uniform color and a fairly symmetric reticular-patchy pattern, though the border is mildly irregular and blotchy; it lacks blue-white veil, atypical vessels or multiple colors, favoring a benign nevus.

Nail unit image with a pale pink nail bed and a faint, uniform grayish band near the distal edge, without irregular pigmented longitudinal bands, Hutchinson sign, or chaotic pigmentation, favoring a benign nail finding.
Large asymmetric light-brown lesion with irregular notched borders, multifocal eccentric brown blotches and patchy atypical network, and central whitish regression-like areas.

An asymmetric, ill-defined light-to-medium brown patch on sun-damaged skin shows irregular pigment distribution, peripheral pink erythema with fine dotted and linear vessels, and whitish regression-like areas, which raises concern for lentigo maligna or early melanoma over a benign keratosis.

Large, asymmetric light-brown lesion with irregular, notched borders, a faint atypical network, pinkish-white regression-like areas and scattered dotted vessels suggest early melanoma (possibly in situ), though a dysplastic nevus remains possible.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, black, blue-gray, pinkish regression areas), irregular peripheral streaks/pseudopods, irregular dots and globules, and blue-white veil-like structureless zones.

Large, ill-defined lesion on sun-damaged skin with irregular brown pigmentation, asymmetric follicular openings, blue-gray peppering/granules centrally, regression-like whitish areas and polymorphous vessels, suggestive of lentigo maligna melanoma.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, multiple colors including a central blue-white veil/blue-gray areas, and an atypical network with irregular peripheral pigmentation.

A small, well-circumscribed pink-red dome-shaped papule with dotted and curved vessels and a few dark gray specks but no pigment network; this looks more like a dermal nevus or basal cell carcinoma, though amelanotic melanoma cannot be ruled out.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (red, blue-gray, black, brown), blue-white veil, milky-red areas, irregular dark blotch, white scar-like regression, and crusting suggest invasive melanoma.

The lesion is asymmetric with an irregular light-brown extension at the periphery, multiple shades of brown, an atypical central network with dark streak-like areas and a few blue-gray dots, though a severely dysplastic nevus remains a close alternative.

Small irregular, asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged skin with blue-gray peppering/granularity, multiple brown-gray-blue colors, and an ill-defined border, suggestive of melanoma in situ or lentigo maligna.

Small but asymmetric, irregularly shaped lesion with eccentric dark brown-black blotch, uneven pigment distribution, and a lighter, irregular orangey-brown upper extension with blurred borders, set on sun-damaged skin.

Facial pigmented macule with a pseudonetwork around follicular openings, ill-defined asymmetric borders, and darker gray-brown dots clustered centrally around follicles, suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Irregular, asymmetric outline with notched borders, uneven brown pigmentation including darker central areas, irregular globules and blotches, on sun-damaged skin with a surgical marking circle around it.

Marked asymmetry with multiple colors (blue-black, purple, dark red, brown), a blue-white veil, irregular dots/globules, white shiny structures, and an irregular brown component with peripheral irregular pigmentation.

A small, fairly well-circumscribed brown lesion with a lobulated, cerebriform/globular pattern, a few dark dots and only mild asymmetry, without an atypical network, regression or blue-white veil, which favors a benign nevus or seborrheic keratosis-like lesion.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark purple-brown center, blue-white veil-like areas, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray), and an irregular light-brown peripheral rim.

Large asymmetric lesion with a pink-red regression-like area containing dotted/polymorphous vessels and milky-red areas, an eccentric dark brown-blue blotch, blue-gray structures, irregular peripheral pigmentation and multiple colors.

Small, fairly symmetric dark brown lesion with a central homogeneous dark area, a regular peripheral brown rim with faint reticular pattern, mildly irregular but well-defined borders, and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric blue-black blotch, irregular peripheral streaks/pseudopods, and an irregular reddish-brown extension with multiple colors.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a darker center, slightly blurred edges and focal blue-gray areas, but no clear atypical network, streaks or regression; most consistent with a benign nevus, though the gray tones and irregular border keep some suspicion.

A large, ill-defined light-to-dark brown lesion with asymmetric, irregular blotches, gray peppering/granularity, patchy white regression-like areas and an atypical network suggest melanoma (likely in situ).

Nail apparatus lesion with a brown longitudinal band, irregular brown pigmentation spilling onto the proximal nail fold (Hutchinson-like sign), periungual pink-white scarring/regression with dotted vessels, and nail plate dystrophy, all of which favor subungual melanoma.

Large, ill-defined lesion with irregular brown pigmentation, asymmetric darker blotch at the edge, pink regression-like areas with dotted/polymorphous vessels and follicular openings suggesting lentigo maligna-type melanoma on sun-damaged skin.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light/dark brown, red, blue-gray), blue-white veil-like areas, irregular dots/globules and an atypical peripheral network.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light/dark brown, blue-gray, pink-red), blue-white veil and regression structures centrally, atypical network with irregular extensions, and irregular notched borders.

Small, asymmetric brown lesion with irregular borders, eccentric darker area, peripheral irregular dots/globules, blue-gray central regression-like structures and a light-brown extension, raising concern for early melanoma, though benign nevus remains possible.

Small (~7 mm), fairly symmetric brown lesion with a reticular network fading at the periphery, a central darker zone with a few dark dots and mild border irregularity, overall most consistent with a dysplastic/compound nevus.

Large lesion extending beyond the field with asymmetric, irregular light-to-dark brown blotches, whitish regression-like zones, a pink-red vascular area and patchy fragmented pigment on sun-damaged skin, raising concern for lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

The lesion is asymmetric and light brown, with an irregular, broken-up pigment network, a central pinkish-white regression-like zone, and irregular peripheral dots and globules scattered at the inferior edge.

A large, poorly defined pink lesion on sun-damaged skin shows dotted and irregular vessels, white scar-like areas, asymmetric light-brown blotches and a focal blue-gray area, which together raise concern for a hypomelanotic or regressing melanoma.
The asymmetric, poorly demarcated lesion shows irregular eccentric brown blotches, blue-gray veil-like and regression-like areas, multiple colors, and a fading irregular border.

A light-brown, fairly regular reticular network forms a peripheral ring around a pinkish, hypopigmented center with fine vessels and no blue-white veil or atypical dots, suggesting a dysplastic or regressing nevus, though the pink center and patchy network keep melanoma in the differential.

An elongated, mildly asymmetric light-brown macule with a fairly uniform tan color and a faint reticular-globular network, plus some irregular borders and subtle pinkish areas that keep dysplastic nevus versus early melanoma in situ in question.

A large, ill-defined pink lesion with a dense, polymorphous reticular and linear-irregular vascular network, scattered faint irregular brown blotches and pigment fragments, and no clear benign pattern, which raises concern for an amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma, though the call is uncertain.
Asymmetric lesion with multiple eccentric, irregular dark brown blotches, a pinkish-red peripheral zone with fine vessels, ill-defined borders, and possible blue-white areas suggest melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric pink macule with fine, evenly spread central brown dots and a faint light-brown periphery, without atypical network, streaks, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, which favors a benign (likely inflamed or dysplastic) nevus, though the pink featureless areas keep some suspicion.

Small (~5 mm) lesion with fairly uniform light-to-medium brown color, a subtle reticular/globular pattern, and only mild border irregularity; there are no blue-white veil, atypical network, or regression structures, which favors a benign nevus, though the slight asymmetry keeps some uncertainty.

A large, hypomelanotic pink-red lesion with a milky-red background, scattered dotted vessels and asymmetric, eccentric irregular brown pigmentation at one edge, which together raise concern for amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma despite the milia-like white dots.

A small, asymmetric, ill-defined light-to-dark brown macule on sun-damaged skin, with eccentric darker pigmentation, a few gray-black dots and faint pinkish areas, is concerning for early melanoma in situ, though a benign lentigo or nevus remains plausible.
Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (tan, brown, dark brown, reddish-pink), irregular dark dots/globules off-center, whitish regression-like areas, and blurred irregular borders.

Small, well-circumscribed, symmetric oval lesion with uniform very dark brown-black pigment, a fairly regular reticular-globular pattern, and sharp borders suggests a dark (hypermelanotic) nevus, though the very dark color keeps some suspicion.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered lesion with multiple colors (brown, pink-red, blue-violet), central regression-like whitish/pink area with dotted vessels, white shiny lines, and peripheral irregular streaks/pseudopods with satellite pigmentation.

Small, dark, fairly compact lesion with a black central blotch and a faint brown peripheral halo, but no clear atypical network or regression; asymmetry and the eccentric smudgy extension keep some suspicion.

Several small lesions, each with a regular fine brown pigment network, symmetric shape, smooth fading edges and no atypical structures, which fits benign nevi; the larger upper lesion's mildly irregular light-brown network adds some uncertainty.

Fairly symmetric lesion with a regular, fine pigment network fading at the periphery, small dots at the edge, and only small central hypopigmented areas without blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic or compound nevus over melanoma.

An asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged follicular (facial/scalp-type) skin with an irregular, scalloped orange-brown border, a central gray-brown zone suggesting regression or lentigo maligna pattern, and multiple colors, though a solar lentigo or lichen planus-like keratosis remains possible.

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular multicomponent pattern, uneven brown to dark-brown and purplish-gray pigmentation, central blue-white/regression-like areas, irregular dots and globules, and blurred, irregular borders.
Small light-brown macule with a fairly symmetric faint reticular pattern and regular borders, but central pinkish regression-like area with dotted vessels adds some concern.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray), blue-white veil and regression areas, irregular dots/globules, and an atypical pigment network extending beyond the frame.

A small asymmetric light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with irregularly distributed dark-brown dots and globules, eccentric red-purple and blue-gray areas, and an ill-defined border, which together favor melanoma over a benign nevus.

Ill-defined pink erythematous patch on densely hairy skin with fine dotted vessels, no pigment network, streaks, or other melanocytic structures, which favors a benign inflammatory or non-melanocytic lesion, though amelanotic melanoma cannot be fully excluded from the image.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped lesion about 8 mm across on sun-damaged skin, with uneven reddish-brown pigmentation, eccentric darker blotches, central regression-like lightening and an irregular notched border, which together favor melanoma (possibly in situ).

A small lesion with a regular brown pigment network at one pole and a central orange-yellow structureless area with scattered red dots, which looks more like crust or hemorrhage from a traumatized nevus than melanoma-specific structures, though the multicomponent pattern keeps melanoma possible.

On chronically sun-damaged skin, this lesion shows multifocal, asymmetric light-brown patches with ill-defined borders and a darker central area with granular, annular-granular pigmentation and scattered red dots, suggesting lentigo maligna, though a solar lentigo or lichen planus-like keratosis remains possible.

A small, fairly well-circumscribed brown lesion with a darker centre and a fairly regular rim of peripheral brown globules (suggesting a growing or Spitz/Reed-type nevus), though the slightly uneven distribution of dots and globules keeps some suspicion.

Asymmetric, multicomponent lesion with irregular atypical network, eccentric blue-black blotch with blue-white structures and scale, regression-like whitish areas, and fragmented irregular borders with satellite pigmented islands.

Small, roughly symmetric brown lesion with a lighter center, peripheral brown dots and fairly regular borders on sun-damaged, erythematous, telangiectatic skin, most consistent with a benign nevus or solar lentigo, though the peripheral granularity keeps melanoma from being fully excluded.

Large irregular light-to-dark brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an atypical network, central blue-gray peppering and dots, regression-like whitish areas, and ill-defined asymmetric borders, suggestive of lentigo maligna melanoma.

A largely amelanotic pink lesion with a central blue-white, milky-red structureless area, irregular dotted vessels, surface scale and irregular light-brown peripheral blotches is suspicious for amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma, though Bowen's disease or BCC remain possible.

Small, fairly uniform light-brown lesion with an eccentric darker focus and fine peppered dots on sun-damaged skin with a background vascular network, but no atypical network, streaks, or blue-white veil.

An ill-defined, asymmetric light-to-dark brown macule on sun-damaged skin shows irregular pigmentation and gray-brown granules (peppering) centrally, which raises concern for lentigo maligna, though a regressing solar lentigo or lichen planus-like keratosis remains possible.
Asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, black, blue-gray), irregular eccentric dark blotch, regression-like whitish areas, irregular dots/globules and uneven borders.

A featureless pink, amelanotic patch with clustered dotted-to-glomerular and some serpentine vessels and white shiny areas fits Bowen disease or another non-melanocytic lesion more than melanoma, though the polymorphous vessels mean amelanotic melanoma cannot be excluded.

A small asymmetric violet-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin shows granular blue-gray peppering, an irregular extension and surrounding whitish regression-like areas, which raise concern for a regressing melanoma (possibly in situ), though a lichen planus-like keratosis is the main benign alternative.

Large, ill-defined acral lesion with broad parallel bands of light-to-medium brown pigment that may follow the ridges, plus an irregular darker blotch near the top and uneven distribution, which raises concern for acral melanoma.
An asymmetric, irregularly bordered brown lesion with uneven pigment, dotted and polymorphous red vessels, white scar-like regression areas and a surrounding pink erythematous zone.
Fairly regular, symmetric brown reticular network that fades gradually at the periphery, with only mild central hyperpigmentation and no blue-white veil, regression structures or atypical vessels.

A raised pink, mostly amelanotic nodule shows polymorphous dotted, glomerular and serpentine vessels on a milky-red/white background, with bluish-white veil-like areas and irregular eccentric brown pigment, a pattern suspicious for hypomelanotic nodular melanoma.
